text: 🇲🇽✊ "The biggest corruption in the past was the big distributors. They outsourced the whole system, and they charged eight times what the system cost." That way, capacities of the Mexican State are built that were lost during the whole neoliberal period." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 23, 2026 A reporter asked about supplies being stolen and resold. Sheinbaum said such cases exist and must be reported, but they can't be generalized: most health workers save lives every day. She called the attacks a paid campaign. Under the old model, even hospital pharmacies were run by private firms, on 10- to 15-year contracts, with kickbacks to officials.

text: 🇲🇽⚖️ "Zero privileges. Let us never forget where we come from. We come from a movement that fought against the privileges of a few. It cannot be that you get to where you are and your objective is privilege." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 23, 2026 A reporter asked about senators who requested access to the protocol lounge at Mexico City's international airport, criticized online as VIP treatment. "We would not lend them. Of course not." Later in the same conference, Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco confirmed the request had been made, and that the Foreign Ministry said no. Her message to legislators: "Don't forget where you come from."

🇲🇽🔍 "It is the lowest point since the survey began, 13 years ago. In other words, people feel safer, according to INEGI." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 23, 2026 INEGI's urban public security survey (ENSU) found that 58.1% of adults in 91 cities felt unsafe in their city in September 2026. That is 4.9 points lower than a year earlier and the lowest since the survey began in 2013. The drop was larger among men. "Among women, the perception of insecurity is higher, and there we still have to keep working every day." She congratulated the security cabinet and the operational forces: Security, Defense, Navy and National Guard. She also credited the Interior Ministry, which coordinates the program that addresses the causes of violence.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 "Today several stories came out saying Cuban doctors earn more than Mexican doctors. That is false, absolutely false." "It is a direct hiring, and they earn exactly the same as a Mexican doctor. There is no difference. And they help us a lot in many remote places, where there are no specialist doctors who will go." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 23, 2026 Sheinbaum also denied that the Cuban doctors are hired through a company. Figures she read at the mañanera put a doctor's net monthly pay at 36,896 pesos before this year's raise and 39,120 pesos with it. The same day, the government announced that more doctors, nurses and paramedics will be hired across IMSS, ISSSTE and IMSS-Bienestar, with details next week.

text:
🇲🇽📈 <u>Mexico's Economy Grows for a Second Straight Month</u>

Economic activity rose 0.6% in August from July and 3.5% from a year earlier, according to INEGI's IGAE, El Economista reports. Farming, livestock and fishing led with 3.5% monthly growth after falling 1.1% in July. Industry grew 0.6% and services 0.2%. Joan Domene, Oxford Economics' chief Latin America economist, said the August figure supports the recovery of the country's economic activity.

🇲🇽🏥 <u>Mexican Scientists Will Use AI to Fix the Medicine Supply</u>

Sheinbaum presented a nine-member Advisory Council for the Digital Transformation of the Health Sector. Its members are specialists from UNAM, IPN and CIMAT. Deputy Health Secretary Eduardo Clark said the plan uses artificial intelligence to forecast demand, track inventories in real time and trace every delivery to the pharmacy in IMSS and IMSS-Bienestar hospitals. The first results are due in a month, and the new processes start in January 2027.
banner: MEDICINE SUPPLY: AI FROM UNAM, IPN, CIMAT

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>INE Chief Taddei Refuses to Step Down Over Supplier Contracts</u>

At an extraordinary session of the INE General Council, electoral institute president Guadalupe Taddei said she "will not back down." The PRI and Somos MX had demanded her resignation over suspected conflicts of interest with electoral-material suppliers. She blamed political actors and former INE officials for the suspicions, and said the INE will hand over documentation on its use of public money to the competent authorities. Days earlier, Sheinbaum had asked the INE to clear up the allegations.

Her closing line to the parties: "Elections are not won by questioning the institution."

🇲🇽🚔 <u>Fear of Crime in Mexico Hits Its Lowest Level on Record</u>

In September, 58.1% of adults in Mexico's 91 urban areas said they felt unsafe in their city, according to INEGI's ENSU survey. That is the lowest reading since the survey began 13 years ago. It is 1.7 points below June and 4.9 points below September 2025, and 28 cities improved significantly over the year. Sheinbaum credited the Security Cabinet. In San Pedro Garza García, only 5.8% feel unsafe.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Trump Says a Deal With Mexico Is "Very Close" as Ebrard Pushes to Cut Car and Steel Tariffs</u>

Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard, in Washington after being called in by the US government, reported progress in talks to cut the Section 232 tariffs on Mexican cars, steel and aluminum. Those tariffs stand at 25% on vehicles and 50% on steel and aluminum. Trump followed: "We are very close to a deal with Mexico. It will be a very good deal, hopefully for them, but it will be very good for us."

Sheinbaum has already drawn the line: "We cannot negotiate anything that is outside our Constitution and our laws."
